messages.subject: example model debugging session
parts:
I thought some others might be interested in
following along the steps I used to debug Song's
program.

The moral of the story is that:

(a) NUTS is always right :-) [this is a corollary
to Matt always being right],

(b) plot your data to make sure you have the right
model, and

(c) build up complexity from smaller working models.

More details below.

On 9/26/12 10:51 PM, Song S. Qian wrote:
> Sorry for the inconvenience. The dumped data file and a text file of the model are attached.

Not your fault at all -- we hadn't even specified what
we wanted. Yours was about the fifth data set in which
I struggled with R to get what I needed (I'm not very
good with R!).

There was some back and forth on data and why I needed
was
-- the model in a text file, and
-- just the dump file from R,

Not the dump of the whole input.data structure, just the variables.
Just like the input format for JAGS and BUGS, by the way!
But I guess that all gets hidden by the R interfaces.

I don't know how to make these instructions findable
and easy to follow for other users. Any suggestions?

Also, that model didn't declare the constraints,
but I think an intermediate one did, so I fixed that first.

Then I got the same error as Song, even with the constraints.

So the next thing I tried was simplifying the model to
just a Poisson:

for (i in 1:NOBS) {
real lambda;
real pi;
lambda <- exp(beta1 - beta2 * x[i] + beta3 * log(x[i]));
pi <- inv_logit(alpha1 + alpha2 * x[i]);
Y[i] ~ poisson(lambda);

This seemed to work OK.


I then plotted x vs. Y (the predictors and outcomes) in
in R (just plot(x,Y)) and it looks pretty difficult to
fit. At around x = 10, all the Y are 0 other than one huge
outlier. Then below x = 10, you get lots of values
with high Y, but there doesn't seem to have much relation
to x.

If I run a lot of iterations (100K+), I get down to around
a total (unnormalized) log prob of around -1000. NUTS
has to start out with small steps, but eventually finds
its stride and winds up sampling pretty quickly (14s for
50K warmup iterations and 50K samples).

I then moved to making the zero-inflation binomial pi a
parameter with a uniform prior on (0,1) and went
back to the mixture model. It fit even better, at around
-900 log probability.

Then I just reparameterized as an intercept only logistic
regression inv_logit(alpha1). This works just fine, too.

When I added the alpha2 * x[i] term back in with alpha2
constrained to be positive, all was lost. I realized
it was going the wrong way from the plot, got rid of
the constraint, then ran and everything looks OK.
It fits a bit better than the intercept-only regression.

I've attached the revised model for comparison.

You'll notice I've also dropped the truncations, which
aren't necessary when the variable's constrained and
the truncation points are constant (it only contributes
a constant multipler to the log posterior, which we don't
need for HMC/NUTS).

- Bob
